meta.title: The one list
meta.authority: This file is the ONLY record of what is done. Prose docs explain the work; they do not track it.
meta.howToRead:
pnpm backlog          — the working view (open + blocked)
pnpm backlog --lane owner — one lane
pnpm check:backlog    — prove every row against the tree (runs in CI)
rules: A row's status is proven by its verify probe, not by memory. If they disagree, CI fails.
A probe must measure the CONSEQUENCE in the tree, never restate the row's own title. A probe that passes by existing is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs.
Manual rows never fail the build (ADR-970). They carry evidence + a checked date and go stale loudly.
Parked rows are not probed: 'you could do this now' is true of everything parked and therefore says nothing.
Never delete a probe to make CI pass. That is precisely how the previous five master lists drifted.

lanes.owner: Config or a decision. No code unblocks it.
lanes.program: A named multi-phase program. Needs a scheduling decision, not a start.
lanes.hygiene: Debt in the record or the instruments.

entries.title: The .dark [data-skin="midnight"] selector never matches on the <html> path
entries.detail: A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself. app/layout.tsx stamps data-skin on documentElement (the global skin preview path, including marketing); only the shell root is a descendant. So midnight-dark renders a MIXTURE: the generic .dark palette with midnight's light-mode overrides under it. The comment at app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite, which is why it survived. One selector, but it repaints every midnight-dark surface, so it wants its own pass with a baseline recapture.
entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Non-vacuity proven by the parent, not taken on report: reverting to the descendant-only selector fails skin-dom-selectors.test.ts with 'A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself'. The second half matters more than the row did — authoring the selector LIST would have silently dropped the block from check-contrast's resolver, which scored the raw prelude and returned null for any comma-separated selector, so the contrast gate would have kept printing green for midnight-dark while measuring nothing there (ADR-970). Fixed in the same pass; selectorWeight now scores each part of a list independently.

entries.title: The app shell statically imports the entire admin module registry

It reaches crypto-browserify/stream-browserify: 406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip on EVERY authed page, verified as a blocking script tag in served HTML. Fix: next/dynamic per module, import module IDS not components, and add import 'server-only' to lib/journey-plans and lib/practices so the class fails the build. NOTE: needs a route-level first-load measurement, which the agent container cannot produce (next build fails page-data collection without service-role creds).

entries.title: Sentry no longer ships to routes with no DSN configured
entries.detail: The static `import * as Sentry` is gone; the SDK is now reached through a dynamic import gated on process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN — the one env form the browser can resolve, since Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time. The server-only SENTRY_DSN fallback is deliberately NOT consulted here because it is never inlined into the browser bundle and could only read undefined. The hard part was the export contract: Next reads onRouterTransitionStart off this module's namespace and calls it on every client navigation, so it MUST stay defined with Sentry off — it is now a stable wrapper delegating to an async-loaded hook, with a .catch that leaves it a no-op if the chunk fails, because monitoring must never take down the app it monitors. Stated cost: a navigation in the first few ms of a configured session may go untraced. VERIFIED BEYOND THE ONE FILE (the searchSiteIcons lesson): every importer of lib/observability/sentry was enumerated — only sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts import it statically, both server/edge runtimes, and lib/maps/diagnostics.ts deliberately reads the value without importing. No client component pulls it, so the SDK cannot re-enter the baseline chunk by a side door.
entries.notes: Artifact-verified 2026-08-17, not inferred: built with no DSN and read the emitted chunks. The 236,682-byte Sentry SDK chunk appears in 0 of 4,149 client entry lists across all 404 page_client-reference-manifest.js files, and the baseline chunk in rootMainFiles contains only the gated async loader. app/error, app/global-error and components/ui/route-error.tsx still import the SDK statically; Turbopack keeps those in async groups, so they are not a baseline regression and were deliberately left alone.

entries.title: Decide how /discover index pages resolve isAuthed without killing ISR
entries.detail: Three index pages call createClient() → cookies() purely for an isAuthed boolean, killing ISR and adding an auth round trip per crawl. DO NOT 'just remove the auth read' — it silently breaks sign-in destinations: isAuthed feeds communityHref, and proxy.ts builds its redirect by rewriting the pathname and NEVER setting next=, so the destination is lost. Two real options: (a) make the proxy set next= (strictly better product behaviour but changes where every signed-out deep link lands across 122 protected routes), or (b) resolve isAuthed client-side via the authMode="client" pattern app/discover/layout.tsx already uses. Same decision governs (main)/layout.tsx. Owner call.

entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. Still O(rows), never O(Spaces).

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the batched read pages — rather than the row's words. Backed by app/sitemap.test.ts, which rebuilds the URL list the old per-Space loop would have emitted and requires an exact match, and which was confirmed to FAIL against an unpaged read (expected 1000 to be 1500) before being accepted.

entries.title: scripts/ is typechecked, so the CI guard tests are covered
entries.detail: tsconfig.json no longer excludes scripts/, and **/*.mts joined include. PROVEN FROM THE COMPILER'S OWN RESOLVED CONFIG rather than by reading the JSON: `tsc --showConfig` reports 37 files under scripts/ in the program, including every guard test (backlog-contract, check-adoption, check-bridge, check-contrast, check-creates, check-crm-parity, check-docs-links and the rest). Required allowImportingTsExtensions, because scripts/*.mts run on `node --experimental-strip-types`, where Node does no extension resolution and the explicit `.ts` specifier is runtime-load-bearing; safe under noEmit, and the reason is commented in tsconfig.json rather than left as a bare flag.

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the compiler's RESOLVED PROGRAM contains the scripts/ files — rather than the shape of tsconfig.json. Two earlier versions were wrong in instructive ways. The first was grep-absent /"scripts"/ in tsconfig.json, which a stray scratch config could satisfy with zero files typechecked, and there WAS one in the tree. The second shelled out to `npx`, which reintroduced the exact ambient-tooling dependency the ripgrep fix had just removed — caught by the rg-parity test in backlog-contract.test.ts, which is why that test compares verdicts across a stripped PATH instead of asserting a fixed result. It now calls the repo-local TypeScript binary through node, so it needs nothing on PATH that the guard itself does not already require.

entries.title: Eight ADR numbers were used twice, and the guard was printing a tick over all of them
entries.detail: Closed 2026-08-17. EIGHT collisions, not seven — 9 extra declarations, ADR-090 three times — counted in pure Node rather than trusted from the row. The renumbering is the smaller half. `check:adr` ALREADY EXISTED and was ALREADY WIRED into ci.yml, and it passed on all eight: it compared each count against a frozen GRANDFATHERED map, so it measured 'no worse than the day it shipped' while a reader took the tick for 'no duplicates'. That is ADR-962's vacuous-pass and ADR-970's cannot-fire-honestly in one gate. The map is gone; the rule is now flat and names both claimants' line numbers. Which claimant KEPT each number was decided on repo evidence (COMMS-STRATEGY.md:52 records the double-booking in the repo's own words; DEVELOPMENT-MAP dates; citation weight), not on file position — file order in a number-sorted ledger records the number, not the authoring order. 40 citations repointed, each individually unambiguous.

entries.title: pr-compare-fallback posts the required status without a retry
entries.detail: The workflow exists to break a FOREVER-deadlock: pr-compare is a required context posted by a path-filtered job, so a docs-only PR never gets it and cannot merge, with no admin bypass. Its posting step was a single un-retried curl — so the deadlock-breaker was one transient 503 away from BEING the deadlock, which is exactly what happened on PR #2142. Now retries transient codes only (429/5xx/connection) with backoff, then READS THE STATUS BACK to prove the context exists under the name branch protection consumes.

entries.title: Every Vercel build now throws its cache away: 1.53 GB against a 1.50 GB limit
entries.detail: The build log ends: `Build cache size 1.53 GB exceeds limit of 1.50 GB. Invalidating cache. Next build will start with an empty cache.` It is 2% over, so every build pays a full cold compile and the next one is guaranteed to overflow again — the steady state is no cache at all. Nothing fails, which is the problem: this is a swallowed regression of exactly the shape ADR-1003 names, visible only to someone reading the tail of a green build. It also compounds the artifact risk the deploy-safety rules exist for, since a cold build is the slowest path to the ENOSPC cliff. Fix by trimming what enters the cache, not by assuming the limit will move. Measure first: the same log reports input source code at 2,890 MB and node_modules at 948 MB.

verify.evidence: Observed 2026-08-17 in the build log for deployment HFda7FHVybGxMCM6BKBhwxzcGAzy (commit 67bd24a): 'Build cache size 1.53 GB exceeds limit of 1.50 GB. Invalidating cache.' Not repo-probeable — the cache size is a property of the Vercel build, not of the tree.

entries.title: Create the stable Crew product and set STRIPE_PRODUCT_CREW, or every subscriber mints their own
entries.detail: Crew is pay-what-you-want, so createMembershipCheckout mints an ad-hoc inline recurring price per checkout at the member's chosen amount. It parents those prices to process.env.STRIPE_PRODUCT_CREW specifically 'so the ad-hoc prices roll up under ONE product instead of littering the dashboard with a product per subscriber', and falls back to inline product_data when unset. The live account has ZERO products, so the variable cannot be pointing at a valid one: as it stands every Crew subscriber creates a separate Stripe product. Fix is one product plus one env var, and it is worth doing BEFORE the first Crew signup rather than cleaning up afterwards. .env.example:194 already reserves the key.
